title: Recognition Chain
description: The seven-link recognition chain instantiated for one system, with a status per link. The status is the only input the gating rule consumes. Statuses are assigned by hand with evidence locators and committed before any detector is run.

declared_kind.description: The analyst's committed classification. The generator computes a kind independently from link statuses; a mismatch is reported, never silently reconciled.

committed_before_detection.description: True if this chain was fixed before detectors were run over the corpus (paper §10.1).

annotator_agreement.description: Per-link agreement between independent annotators. Paper §13 records that this has not been run; the field exists so that its absence is visible rather than assumed.

status.description: internal: the system specifies the link and it is carried out under the system's own authority. external: the link occurs but is neither specified nor governed by the system. absent: the system has no such link at all.

filler.description: What occupies the link in this domain, e.g. 'judge, official'.

evidence.description: Locators supporting the status assignment. Required in practice for any chain used in the empirical design.

specification.description: Optional. Whether the system SPECIFIES this link, as distinct from whether it performs it. `status` is the performance question and is the only field the gating rule consumes. The two come apart at exactly the place the framework cares about: a diagnostic manual specifies criteria in full (specification internal) but does not apply them under its own authority (status external). Recording only one of the two makes the criteria layer of a classification look either thinner or thicker than it is.
